predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: Old Hormuz (Naband) on the mainland near Minab

ledger.x: Bridge at confidence 1 (page silent on the year): the kingdom was founded 'after the collapse of the Buyid kingdom' in the 11th century by Muhammad Diramku, who emigrated from Oman to the Iranian coast; the Kerman Seljuk emir Badr Isa of Hormuz had submitted to Qavurt before 1073 (Qavurt page).
Undated, placed at 1300 (Persian overlordship cast off): 'The Hurmuzi rulers developed Qalhat on the Omani coast in order to control both sides of the entrance to the Persian Gulf.'
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1301: the capital moves to Jarun, the island of Hormuz.
1301: the court moves from Old Hormuz (Naband) to the island of Jarun.

September 1507: Afonso de Albuquerque lands on the island of Hormuz ('In September 1507, the Portuguese Afonso de Albuquerque landed on the island'); the Hormuz Island page: he 'captured the island in 1507'.
1515: the Portuguese take Ormuz ('After seizing Hormuz in 1515'; 'from 1515 to 1622') and the kingdom becomes their vassal.
1515: Hormuz island passes to the Portuguese, who built the Fort of Our Lady of the Conception there (Hormuz Island page); the portuguese-empire dossier records the conquest in 1515.
1622: the Safavids, helped by the English, conquer the kingdom ('conquered the kingdom in 1622'; infobox 'Safavid conquest: 1622').
1622: the kingdom ends; Shah Abbas I 'shifted the Gulf trade to Bandar Abbas, located on the mainland'.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Hormuz
wars.outcome: Albuquerque landed on the island in September 1507; the Portuguese occupied Ormuz in 1515 and held it to 1622 with the king as vassal.

wars.name: Portuguese invasion of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Hormuz page says Hormuz 'jointly participated in the 1521 invasion of Bahrain that ended Jabrid rule'; the Jabrids page says Muqrin fell in battle in Bahrain against a Portuguese invasion and does not mention Hormuz.

wars.name: Capture of Ormuz (1622)
wars.outcome: Anglo-Persian forces took the Portuguese garrison at Hormuz Island in 1622; the Hormuz page says the Safavids 'conquered the kingdom in 1622' with English help.

certainty.note: A coastal city-state: a disc round Minab and, from 1301, the island of Hormuz and Qalhat on the Omani coast; no frontier on any page opened, and the reach to Bahrain and Muscat is undated.
